clue.text: Bloodsucker's plot to arrange secret hearing

parts.note: a plot of ground in a garden, as in a flower bed
to bug a room is to plant a hidden microphone so talk can be overheard

explanation.surface: A spy's scheme to set up an eavesdropping session is the work of a bloodsucker.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Bloodsucker stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The bedbug is a small insect that feeds on human blood at night, a literal bloodsucker.

clue.text: In flight, even case may disappear

indicators.note: letters in flight are scattered and fleeing, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suitcase put on a plane might go missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In flight' sets up the luggage picture but signals that EVENCASE is to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To evanesce is to fade away or vanish, a literary verb for disappearing.

clue.text: Stole track for sporting event

parts.note: a boa is a long scarf of feathers or fur, a kind of stole
to trace someone is to track them down

explanation.surface: Following a fur wrap to the races, as if at a sporting occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boat Race is a famous annual rowing contest, a fixture of the British sporting calendar.

clue.text: Explain away shiny appearance maiden perhaps presents

parts.note: gloss is a lustrous surface sheen
in cricket a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored, so maiden is one example of an over

explanation.surface: A young woman's polished look gives an excuse for her conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled; a maiden is one with no runs scored. 'presents' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To gloss over a problem is to explain it away or play it down so it escapes notice.

clue.text: Good offices in a country without interesting quality

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: Aus is a common abbreviation for Australia
spice is what adds interest or zest

explanation.surface: Diplomats working in a foreign land find the place dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense outside, a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the auspices of someone means with their patronage and support, their good offices.

clue.text: One who runs after clients wanting immediate attention

definitions.text: One who runs after clients wanting immediate attention

parts.words: One who runs after clients wanting immediate attention
parts.note: read as a lawyer chasing accident victims, those who needed emergency help, in hope of compensation work

explanation.surface: A busy professional pursues customers who need urgent service.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a disparaging term for a lawyer who pursues accident victims as clients, literally following emergency vehicles.

clue.text: Fruit when cut keeps good colour

indicators.note: one piece keeps the other within it, holding it inside
a cut word loses its final letter here

parts.note: a pimento is a sweet red pepper, botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: A trimmed piece of fruit retains a fine hue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the last letter of PIMENTO, giving PIMENT, which 'keeps' G inside. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a substance that gives colour, such as paint powder or the colouring in skin.

clue.text: Author (no beginner) in intelligence agency has standards

indicators.note: placed within the letters of the agency's name

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: the word for author loses its opening letter

parts.note: an author is a writer

explanation.surface: A novelist working undercover for the spooks has principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no beginner' drops the first letter of the author word; 'in' puts the remainder inside the agency. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the standards or tests by which something is judged; the word is the plural of criterion.

clue.text: Enlightenment: it requires holy book I lost

parts.note: it is a dated word for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

indicators.note: the letter named before it is lost from the book's name

parts.note: Genesis is the first book of the Bible
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seeker after wisdom finds it needs scripture, though they have lost themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal (SA) is an old crossword favourite. 'lost' removes one I from GENESIS, leaving GENESS. 'requires' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sageness is the state of being sage, wise or enlightened, so it equals enlightenment or wisdom.

clue.text: Tom has a curry in the cellar

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
to curry a horse is to groom it with a comb

explanation.surface: Tom eats a spicy dish down in the basement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curry' wants to be food; it is the grooming verb, as with a currycomb. 'has' and 'in the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground burial chamber, loosely an underground vault or cellar.

clue.text: Getting on with gang that's criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Growing old in the company of a band of crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' gives IE, which joins GANG as the pool for 'criminal' to rearrange. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageing means growing older, and getting on is an idiom for advancing in years.

clue.text: Publicity is part of true revenge

indicators.note: becoming part of a word by sitting inside its letters

parts.note: real means true or genuine
PR stands for public relations, publicity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Media coverage is one element of genuine payback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' signals a container: the publicity word and 'is' sit inside the word for true.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is an act of retaliation, revenge taken for an injury.

clue.text: Estate said to be humble

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the estate word gives the sound of another word

parts.note: a demesne is land held by a lord as his own estate

explanation.surface: A landed property is reputed to be modest.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMESNE is pronounced like DEMEAN. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity, to humble or degrade them.

clue.text: Weird sisters chased by social worker to take the pledge

indicators.note: chased by means followed, so the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: the Weird Sisters are Macbeth's three witches, a coven
the ant is a social insect, and worker ants are its labourers

explanation.surface: Witches pursued by a welfare officer swear off drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' wants to be a welfare officer; it is the ANT, a social insect. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To covenant is to make a formal binding agreement, to pledge oneself to something.

clue.text: New hearing aid used for a close call

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing
a thing is any object used as an aid or tool

explanation.surface: A fresh device for the deaf turns out to be a narrow escape.
explanation.walkthrough: The hearing aid reads whimsically as an 'ear thing'. 'for a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, something that almost went wrong: a close call.

clue.text: Only a short reflection from Jeremiah

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the letters are read backwards
letters taken out from within the prophet's name

explanation.surface: A brief meditation drawn from the prophet Jeremiah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a short ... from' takes EREM from inside Jeremiah; 'reflection' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere as an adjective means nothing more than, simply or only.

clue.text: Military equipment that's left after end of war with China

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Arms remaining after a war ends, with China involved.
explanation.walkthrough: China = mate is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate). 'after' and 'with' just join the pieces; 'end of' takes the last letter of war.
explanation.definitionFit: Materiel is the stock of weapons, vehicles and supplies used by an armed force.

clue.text: Career girl, not one for a lot of coming and going

definitions.text: a lot of coming and going

parts.note: to career is to rush along headlong

indicators.note: not drops the following named letter from the word

parts.note: a houri is a beautiful maiden of the Muslim paradise
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman with a job turns down a lot of socialising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career girl' reads as a working woman, but 'Career' is the verb rush. HOURI without I gives HOUR. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rush hour is the busy time of day when commuters travel, with crowds coming and going.

clue.text: Bachelor knocking back spring rolls

indicators.note: knocking something back sends it in reverse, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A single man downing drinks at a spring resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' sounds like drinking but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Baps are soft bread rolls, a British word for a type of roll.

clue.text: Boobs showing in rational dress

definitions.meaning: blunders or mistakes, as in a bad gaffe
Victorian name for women's reform clothing, notably loose baggy trousers worn for cycling

explanation.surface: Errors are visible in sensible clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boobs' teases with a cheeky sense but means blunders. 'showing in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are both blunders (British slang) and the baggy knickerbockers of the Victorian rational dress movement.

clue.text: Husband wearing nose peg turning off gas

indicators.note: the outer letters wear the inserted letter, holding it inside
turning suggests the letters are twisted into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A man with a clip on his nose avoids the fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning off' rearranges NOSEPEG to POSGENE; 'wearing' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosgene is a poisonous gas used as a chemical weapon in the First World War.

clue.text: No alternative in riot but to take a quick drop

indicators.note: no here means taking away, so the alternative word is removed

parts.note: a free-for-all is a disorderly brawl, a riot
or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: With no option left during unrest, someone simply jumps.
explanation.walkthrough: FREE-FOR-ALL without OR leaves the answer. 'in' and 'but to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To free-fall is to drop through the air before a parachute opens, a fast descent.

clue.text: Pincers to deal with mushrooms

parts.note: for in the sense of concerning, intended to handle, as in a remedy for colds
ceps are a kind of edible wild mushroom

explanation.surface: Tongs for handling fungi.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceps are a pincer-like instrument for gripping, used by surgeons and dentists.

clue.text: Former king protected by irascible counsel

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: one piece is shielded inside another

parts.note: hot as in hot-tempered, quick to anger
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch is guarded by a bad-tempered adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' puts the king inside the word for irascible.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to urge or earnestly advise, to counsel strongly.

clue.text: Where shoots may be forced to rise early

definitions.text: Where shoots may be forced to rise early

parts.words: Where shoots may be forced to rise early
parts.note: read as a heated glasshouse where gardeners force young plants to grow ahead of season

explanation.surface: A place where young hunters are made to get up at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated greenhouse is used to force plants to grow faster than they would outdoors.

clue.text: Person in the way I took the lead and flattened

indicators.note: taking the lead means going in front, so the letter comes first
one piece sits inside the abbreviation for road

parts.note: RD is short for road, a way
one means a person, as in one should

explanation.surface: Someone on the road became leader and was crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took the lead' puts I in front; 'in' places the person inside the road abbreviation. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironed means pressed flat, smoothed with an iron or levelled out.

clue.text: Shaken, as he drives appallingly

indicators.note: driving appallingly means swerving all over, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A passenger is rattled because the man at the wheel is terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: HEDRIVES rearranged gives the answer. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shivered means trembled or shook, so it can stand for shaken in the sense of quivered.

clue.text: Birds hear sound of cat, one in flowerbed

parts.note: larks are songbirds

indicators.note: what is heard is the noise, standing for a word spelt differently

parts.note: a contented cat purrs

explanation.surface: Songbirds listen to a cat as it rests among the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hear' signals a homophone: the cat's noise is spelt here without its last R.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden flower, a delphinium, so it is one plant found in a flowerbed.

clue.text: What may be trodden on through the smoke

parts.note: the gas is the accelerator pedal, pressed by the foot
per means through or by means of

explanation.surface: Something underfoot seen through the haze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'step on the gas' means press the accelerator. 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasper is old British slang for a cigarette, especially a cheap one.
